rationale: The assistant correctly latched onto the new drawer unit as the key clue and explained overheating protection from restricted airflow, then escalated to an engineer when the customer refused to check under the hob. However the final message drifted away from the ventilation explanation towards 'the internal heat sink is blocked with dust or the fan isn't moving enough air' and 'replace the faulty part', which the evidence does not support and which omits the more fitting suggestion that an installer check the clearances. The suggestion to 'try lifting the hob slightly' on a hardwired built-in unit and an irrelevant 'suitable replacement' model-number panel were minor missteps, but there was no unsafe instruction, fabrication, looping or part recommendation.
